note: Every component whose code the distributions carry, and the license text shipped for it. The texts are copied verbatim into python/licenses/ in each archive. When a component version changes, the corresponding text is refreshed from the origin recorded here.

components.origin: LICENSE in the CPython source distribution
Modules/expat/COPYING in the CPython source distribution
the header comment of Modules/_decimal/libmpdec/mpdecimal.c in the CPython source distribution
the header comment of the vendored HACL* sources under Modules/_hacl in the CPython source distribution
LICENSE.txt in the OpenSSL source distribution
components.linkage: libcrypto and libssl, shipped as shared libraries

components.origin: SQLite ships no license file; this is its published public-domain dedication (https://sqlite.org/copyright.html), matching the disclaimer carried in every SQLite source file
LICENSE in the bzip2 source distribution
LICENSE in the libffi source distribution
COPYING in the XZ Utils source distribution, kept whole because it is the document that records which parts of the package carry which terms
components.note: In 5.4.6 liblzma itself is public domain. The GPLv2 terms the same document mentions cover the xz command-line scripts, which the distributions do not carry.

components.origin: LICENSE in the zstd source distribution
components.note: zstd is dual licensed BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0-only; the BSD terms apply here.

components.origin: pip and all of its vendored packages carry their own license files inside the payload, under lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip-*.dist-info/licenses/
components.linkage: installed into site-packages from the distribution's own ensurepip wheel

components.origin: cpython-android/python.c is modelled on CPython's Programs/python.c and is covered by LICENSE.cpython.txt
libc, libdl, libm, and liblog are provided by the device and are only linked against, never shipped
